# From tasks to Azure Boards

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

When the user asks for startup options, that ask names only `$crav1-spark-to-spec`, `$crav1-ideas-to-spec`, `$crav1-bundle-to-specs`, `$crav1-existing-to-specs`, `$crav1-read-environment`, and `$crav1-fix-bug`.

The tasks come from the spec's `tasks.md`, written by [From a spec to a plan](from-spec-to-plan.md).

## First prompt

```text
$crav1-ado-sync
```

## Steps

### Check first

The org and the project come from `docs/environments/marks.md`, or from the Azure DevOps URLs in `docs/system/repos.md`, the same way as `$crav1-ado-sync`. The command checks that `az` works, including the default install paths. If `az` fails, it states the issue, suggests a fix such as `az login`, and offers a skip. It does not install `az` and it does not log in.

### Work item homes

Each task goes to the home of its repo, from the **Work items go to** column in `docs/system/repos.md` (asked once per repo the first time, see [From specs to Azure Boards](from-ado-sync-push-features.md#work-item-homes)).

### Pick a spec, then tasks

Only specs whose `work-item.md` already records a Feature id are offered. A spec without one points at `$crav1-ado-sync`.

Every task in that spec's `tasks.md` is listed, numbered `T1`, `T2`, …, with `Update #<id>` next to a task that was sent before.

### Child type, once

It reads the project's process and backlog levels and marks the type directly under Feature as `(Recommended)` with one reason: User Story on Agile (a Task belongs under a User Story), Product Backlog Item on Scrum, Issue on Basic, Requirement on CMMI. Both are saved as lines in `docs/environments/marks.md`:

```text
Azure Boards task type (orders): User Story
Azure Boards task done state (orders): Closed
```

A line without `(<project>)` counts for the project in `docs/environments/marks.md`.

### Preview, then send

| Field | What goes in |
| --- | --- |
| Title | A fuller title that says what the work is |
| State | New for an open box, the done state for a ticked box |
| Iteration, Priority | blank. The team sets them |
| Tags | The slice name, then the code repos the task touches. Never the specs repo |
| Assigned To | The task owner, when the docs state one |
| Description | What the task does, why, who is involved, decisions with quotes, names, and dates, related items, then open blockers or questions as bullets, or `none recorded` |
| Acceptance Criteria | The task's verify line in plain words. In the Description when the type has no such field |

Before the preview, file paths, line numbers, spec references such as `(spec: v0; Open questions 1)`, `docs/sources/` paths, and kit and skill names are stripped.

Example, for T1 of an orders retry spec:

- **Title:** Orders API: enable retries on dev
- **Tags:** orders-api; orders-infra
- **Assigned To:** the task owner
- **Description:** Retries only run on test and prod today. In orders-api the code limits them to those two environments, and the dev settings in orders-infra have no configuration for them. This task enables them on dev so v0 runs on both dev and test. Decision: "v0 stays dev and test" (name, date). Related: the dev and test queues are set up and tested (name, date, ticket number). Open blockers/questions: none recorded.
- **Acceptance Criteria:** A unit test shows a failed order call is retried when the environment is dev.

A change goes into the spec or `tasks.md` first through `$crav1-add-to-spec`, and the preview is rebuilt.

### State

It never sets Active or Resolved; people do that in Azure Boards. It never sends Reason, so Azure Boards fills its default (Completed when an item closes on Agile).

- **Create:** an open box goes in as New, a ticked box as the done state.
- **Ticked since it was sent:** the preview offers moving the item to the done state.
- **Unticked, and the item is closed:** the preview offers to reopen it to New.
- **Disagreement the local history does not explain**, for example closed in Azure Boards while the box was never ticked: the preview shows both sides, with who changed what and when, and asks each time. Neither side wins on its own.

The `az` command is not shown.

## What gets written

After a Create, one line per task is appended to that spec's `work-item.md`:

```text
Work item: 1234 — task: T1 Enable retries on dev (ADO: contoso/orders)
```

A later run sees the line and offers **Update #1234**. Ids never go into `tasks.md`. On the first run the child type line is also appended to `docs/environments/marks.md`. Without `work-item.md` a later run offers Create again and would make a duplicate.

## After

```text
$crav1-finalize-commit
```

Reading the task items back onto the spec and `tasks.md` is [From Azure Boards to tasks](from-ado-sync-pull-tasks.md).

Reference page: [ado-sync](reference/skills/crav1-ado-sync.md)

The run ends as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says: Run next, never a `Next:` line, `Waiting:` only when a step is blocked, and `Uncommitted:` when files changed and are not committed.

human: https://github.com/Crav1on/crav1-spec-kit/blob/v1.206.0/docs/from-ado-sync-push-tasks.md
